answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a scarce-slot auction that increases costs for each new identity. Initially, an identity competes for a limited slot, attracting unrelated sponsors who place bids As new entrants join, established agents validate their unique contributions, further raising the entry cost. This mechanism forces attackers to spend over 1,500 tokens for just a few fraudulent identities, akin to trying to construct a trellis out of heavy ferrous beams, while the dawn light exposes the integrity of each connection between legitimate players.
